source.stem:
The table describes four different resistance wires. They are all made from the same metal.
Which wire has the smallest resistance?

options.text: length of diameter of wire / m 2.0; wire / mm 1.0
length of diameter of wire / m 2.0; wire / mm 1.5
length of diameter of wire / m 3.0; wire / mm 1.0
length of diameter of wire / m 3.0; wire / mm 1.5

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: For equal-sized wires carrying the same current, the more conductive wire produces more heat.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: Nichrome always produces more heat than copper, regardless of how much current flows through each.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: The nichrome wire must become warm first; its warmth then makes electric current flow.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: Only nichrome wires become warm when electric current flows.

intelligence.enrichment: When electric current flows through a conductor, resistance to the flow produces heat; different conducting materials can produce different amounts of heat. current flows through the conductor -> resistance opposes the current -> heat is generated -> the wire feels warm The learner correctly applies this rule: When electric current flows through a conductor, resistance to the flow produces heat; different conducting materials can produce different amounts of heat. A wire becomes warm simply because the cell is connected, not because current meets resistance in the wire.
